name: The entire history of {X} explained
description: Chronological compression of a subject's full history — from origin to present, in one episode. Promises completeness ('the entire history') and clarity ('explained'). Works across formats: documentary, educational, sleep, and even comedy with a wry framing.
openingDevice: Open with the most arresting fact or earliest concrete moment in the history of {X}. Hook with specificity (a year, a name, a place). Then immediately frame the full arc: 'In this episode we'll travel from [earliest moment] to [present state] — every meaningful turn in between.' Set the scope explicitly so the listener knows what to expect.
bodyStructure: Chapter 1: Origins — the earliest available record or known beginning of {X}, with its full context
Chapter 2: Foundations — early developments, the first stable form, who the early shapers were
Chapters 3-{lastButOne}: Eras — each chapter is one major era or transition in the history of {X}, with the dates, names, and turning points that defined it. Move chronologically
Chapter {last}: Present + legacy — where {X} is now, what continues, what's been lost, what the listener should carry forward
closingDevice: Close by zooming out — the broad arc the listener just travelled, the through-line from origin to now, what the next chapter (which they may live to see) might look like.
